tags.gist: Welcomes FDA's risk-based effort, believing AI can improve access, efficiency and outcomes if technology never outpaces patient safety.
Would automate low-risk administrative functions while regulating clinical uses by the seriousness of the decision, patient vulnerability and consequences of error.
Wants diagnosis, prescribing, treatment planning, referrals, triage and escalation to always require licensed clinician approval, with stricter standards for children.
Wants enforceable requirements rather than voluntary principles, beginning with independent testing before market and recurring audits by third parties.
Wants permanent tamper-resistant decision logs recording inputs, outputs, actions, model version and the individuals responsible for review.
Wants continuous monitoring for accuracy, bias, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, model drift and unequal outcomes across populations.
Wants incident reporting made mandatory and procedures defined to immediately disable, roll back or recall unsafe AI functions.
Wants financial penalties, corrective-action requirements and FDA enforcement whenever developers or provider organizations fall short of their obligations.
Wants every material change documented and assessed, and independently revalidated before broader deployment when it could affect performance or safety.
Wants developers, manufacturers, organizations and users given defined responsibilities so none can shift accountability after an adverse event.
Says public trust depends on clear boundaries, measurable standards, independent oversight and real consequences for violations.
Wants innovation to advance with accountability, transparency and safety built in, and offers to work with FDA on a durable framework.
Repeats in the attachment its welcome for a risk-based framework that keeps technology from outpacing patient safety.
Repeats that clinical decisions such as diagnosis, prescribing and triage must always get licensed clinician approval, with enhanced oversight for vulnerable patients.
Repeats the call for required independent testing before market and recurring audits by third parties as enforceable guardrails.
Repeats the call for tamper-resistant decision logs and continuous monitoring for accuracy, bias, cybersecurity, drift and unequal outcomes.
Repeats the call for mandatory incident reporting and procedures to disable, roll back or recall unsafe functions.
Repeats that material changes, including foundation model or agentic capability changes, need independent revalidation before broader deployment.
Repeats that each participant needs defined responsibilities so accountability cannot be shifted after an adverse event.
Repeats that trust requires boundaries, standards, independent oversight and consequences, with innovation advancing alongside accountability.
